1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""A list command for Pilot (ADR 0010). Pilot writes one JSON run message on stdin and closes it; the program prints
3	JSON lines on stdout: here one list message, whose rows Pilot filters as you type. Python 3.9 stdlib only, as macOS's
4	/usr/bin/python3; a list must answer within 2 s."""
5	import json
6	import sys
7	
8	
9	def send(message):
10	    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(message, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
11	
12	
13	def items(run):
14	    rows = [("Alpha", "the first row"), ("Beta", "the second row"), ("Gamma", "the third row")]
15	    send({"type": "list", "items": [
16	        {"id": title.lower(), "title": title, "subtitle": words,
17	         "actions": [{"type": "copy", "text": title, "title": "Copy"},
18	                     {"type": "hud", "text": "%s: %s" % (title, words), "title": "Say it"}]}
19	        for title, words in rows]})
20	
21	
22	def main():
23	    try:
24	        run = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
25	    except ValueError:
26	        send({"type": "error", "text": "got a run message it could not read"})
27	        return
28	    command = run.get("command")
29	    if command == "items":
30	        items(run)
31	    else:
32	        send({"type": "error", "text": "has no command %s" % command})
33	
34	
35	if __name__ == "__main__":
36	    main()

delta.text:
I made an "Open Ports" list extension and installed it. It lists the TCP ports this Mac is listening on, with the program name and PID for each. Return copies the port number.

To open it, type "Open Ports" in Hyper+Space and filter by the port you want.

The extension is in `/tmp/pilot-ext/demo/open-ports`. It calls `/usr/sbin/lsof` with a 1.5 s timeout and reports an error row if that fails. The test run returned a list without errors. It listed port 7000 (ControlCenter), but I did not check the rows beyond that.
